entities.name: PMID:25428031
observations: 2015 Journal of the Science of Food and Agriculture study directly tested Shinzami Korean purple-fleshed sweet potato extract in rat hepatic ischaemia-reperfusion injury.
Pretreatment lowered serum AST and ALT and reduced histopathological liver injury versus hepatic ischaemia-reperfusion controls.
The study also tested total anthocyanins extracted from Shinzami; accessible evidence does not establish identical preparation, dose, or composition relative to the whole extract.

entities.name: Shinzami extract
observations: Extract from Korean purple-fleshed sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) administered as pretreatment in a rat hepatic ischaemia-reperfusion model.
Pretreatment increased hepatic glutathione, superoxide dismutase, and glutathione peroxidase activity versus hepatic ischaemia-reperfusion controls.

entities.name: Hepatic ischaemia-reperfusion injury
observations: Rat hepatic ischaemia-reperfusion injury was the experimental model; control animals received hepatic ischaemia-reperfusion without the protective pretreatment.
Reported injury included hepatic architectural distortion, hemorrhage, necrosis, and inflammatory-cell infiltration.

entities.name: Shinzami hepatoprotection
observations: In rats, Shinzami extract pretreatment attenuated hepatic ischaemia-reperfusion damage, with lower AST and ALT, improved antioxidant measures, and less histopathological injury than hepatic ischaemia-reperfusion controls.
Evidence is limited to one directly matching paper; the accessible abstract does not report apoptosis, exact dose, solvent, timing, group sizes, or quantitative effect sizes.
